key_insight: Thermal spray route strongly controls WC-10Co-4Cr coating density and phase retention, with HVOF/HVAF giving the best overall wear resistance while HVAF gives the best corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: For wear- and corrosion-critical components on 304 stainless steel, HVOF/HVAF and DS coatings can markedly outperform APS and the uncoated substrate.
method: Prepared WC-10Co-4Cr coatings on 304 stainless steel by APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Compared microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction/wear behavior, and electrochemical corrosion response.
Identified dominant wear mechanisms from worn-surface observations and load transfer to carbide particles.
evidence_signal: Compared with 304 stainless steel, coatings increased hardness to 771.4–1166.2 HV and reduced wear rate from 36.82×10^-5 to as low as 1.10×10^-5 mm3/N·m, while HVAF showed the best corrosion metrics (Ecorr ≈ -0.37 VSCE, Icorr ≈ 1.75 μA/cm²).
watch_item: Performance rankings are process- and parameter-dependent, so the reported superiority may not transfer directly to different spray settings, substrates, or service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
